sanskrit_shloka: प्रजापतिर्लोकानभ्यतपत्तेषां तप्यमानानां रसान्प्रावृहदग्निं पृथिव्या वायुमन्तरिक्षादादित्यं दिवः ॥ १ ॥
transliteration:
prajāpatir lokān abhyatapat |
               teṣāṃ tapyamānānāṃ rasān prāvṛhat |
               agniṃ pṛthivyāḥ |
               vāyum antarikṣāt |
               ādityaṃ divaḥ || ChUp_4,17.1 ||
translation: Prajāpati brooded over the Regions.—From these thus brooded over, He squeezed their Essences; Agni (Fire) from Earth, Vāyu (Air) from Sky and Āditya (Sun) from Heaven.—(1)

translations.author: VedaPath English
translations.text: Prajāpati brooded over the Regions.—From these thus brooded over, He squeezed their Essences; Agni (Fire) from Earth, Vāyu (Air) from Sky and Āditya (Sun) from Heaven.—(1)

commentaries.author: Adi Shankaracharya Bhashya
commentaries.text: प्रजापतिः लोकानभ्यतपत् लोकानुद्दिश्य तत्र सारजिघृक्षया ध्यानलक्षणं तपश्चचार । तेषां तप्यमानानां लोकानां रसान् साररूपान्प्रावृहत् उद्धृतवान् जग्राहेत्यर्थः । कान् ? अग्निं रसं पृथिव्याः, वायुमन्तरिक्षात् , आदित्यं दिवः ॥

commentaries.author: Adi Shankaracharya Bhashya (Translation)
commentaries.text: Prajāpati brooded over the Regions ;—that is, he performed the penance of contemplation in reference to the Regions, with a view to extracting the essence of these. From these Regions, thus brooded over. He squeezed their essences ,—their most essential parts.—What were these essences?—Fire was the essence of Earth, Air was the essence of the Sky ; and the Sun was the essence of Heaven .—(1).

sanskrit_shloka: स एतास्तिस्रो देवता अभ्यतपत्तासां तप्यमानानाꣳ रसान्प्रावृहदग्नेर्‌ऋचो वायोर्यजूंषि सामान्यादित्यात् ॥ २ ॥
transliteration:
sa etās tisro devatā abhyatapat |
               tāsāṃ tapyamānānāṃ rasān prāvṛhat |
               agner ṛcaḥ |
               vāyor yajūṃṣi |
               sāmāny ādityāt || ChUp_4,17.2 ||
translation: He brooded over these three Deities; from these, thus brooded over, He squeezed their essences; the Ṛk-verses from Āgni , the Yajus-texts from Vāyu , and the Sāma-verses from Āditya .—(2)

translations.author: VedaPath English
translations.text: He brooded over these three Deities; from these, thus brooded over, He squeezed their essences; the Ṛk-verses from Āgni , the Yajus-texts from Vāyu , and the Sāma-verses from Āditya .—(2)

commentaries.author: Adi Shankaracharya Bhashya
commentaries.text: पुनरप्येवमेवाग्न्याद्याः स एतास्तिस्रो देवता उद्दिश्य अभ्यतपत् । ततोऽपि सारं रसं त्रयीविद्यां जग्राह ॥

commentaries.author: Adi Shankaracharya Bhashya (Translation)
commentaries.text: Again, He brooded over these three Divinities,— Agni , Vāyu and Āditya ; and from these He extracted their Essence, in the shape of the Triadic Science (Three Vedas ),—(2)

sanskrit_shloka: स एतां त्रयीं विद्यामभ्यतपत्तस्यास्तप्यमानाया रसान्प्रावृहद्भूरित्यृग्भ्यो भुवरिति यजुर्भ्यः स्वरिति सामभ्यः ॥ ३ ॥
transliteration:
sa etāṃ trayīṃ vidyām abhyatapat |
               tasyās tapyamānāyā rasān prāvṛhat |
               bhūr ity ṛgbhyaḥ |
               bhuvar iti yajurbhyaḥ |
               svar iti sāmabhyaḥ || ChUp_4,17.3 || tad yady ṛkto riṣyed bhūḥ svāheti gārhapatye juhuyāt |
               ṛcām eva tadrasenarcāṃ vīryeṇarcāṃ yajñasya viriṣṭaṃ saṃdadhāti || ChUp_4,17.4 ||
translation: He brooded over this Triadic Science ; and from that, thus brooded over. He squeezed out their essences, Bhūḥ from the Ṛk-verses. Bhūvaḥ from the Yajus-texts , and Svaḥ from the Sāma-verses .—(3)

translations.author: VedaPath English
translations.text: He brooded over this Triadic Science ; and from that, thus brooded over. He squeezed out their essences, Bhūḥ from the Ṛk-verses. Bhūvaḥ from the Yajus-texts , and Svaḥ from the Sāma-verses .—(3)

commentaries.author: Adi Shankaracharya Bhashya (Translation)
commentaries.text: He again brooded over this Triadic Science —the Science of the three Vedas; from this Science, thus brooded over, He squeezed is essence ,— Bhūḥ ,—the first Vyāhṛti —from the Ṛk-verses,— Bhuvaḥ —the second Vyāhṛti —from the Yayuṣ-texts ,—and Svaḥ —the third Vyāhṛti — from the Sāma -verses ,—Thus these three Mahāvyāhṛtis Great Syllables ,—are the essence of all Regions , all Divinities and all Vedas .—At the several sacrificial performances, if the Sacrifice happen to become defective on any point relating to and on account of the Ṛk-Text, one should offer an oblation into the Gārhapatya fire , saying ‘ Bhūḥ Svāhā ’;—this is the extraction for the Defect.—How so? — Thus —this is an adverbial clause.— through the essence of the Ṛk-verses and the virility of the Ṛk-verses, one makes up the defect in the Sacrifice ;—i.e. heals up the wound that had been inflicted upon the Sacrifice, in relation to the Ṛk .—(3-4).

sanskrit_shloka: तद्यदृक्तो रिष्येद्भूः स्वाहेति गार्हपत्ये जुहुयादृचामेव तद्रसेनर्चां वीर्येणर्चां यज्ञस्य विरिष्टं सन्दधाति ॥ ४ ॥
transliteration:
sa etāṃ trayīṃ vidyām abhyatapat |
               tasyās tapyamānāyā rasān prāvṛhat |
               bhūr ity ṛgbhyaḥ |
               bhuvar iti yajurbhyaḥ |
               svar iti sāmabhyaḥ || ChUp_4,17.3 || tad yady ṛkto riṣyed bhūḥ svāheti gārhapatye juhuyāt |
               ṛcām eva tadrasenarcāṃ vīryeṇarcāṃ yajñasya viriṣṭaṃ saṃdadhāti || ChUp_4,17.4 ||
translation: He brooded over this Triadic Science ; and from that, thus brooded over. He squeezed out their essences, Bhūḥ from the Ṛk-verses. Bhūvaḥ from the Yajus-texts , and Svaḥ from the Sāma-verses .—(3)

translations.author: VedaPath English
translations.text: He brooded over this Triadic Science ; and from that, thus brooded over. He squeezed out their essences, Bhūḥ from the Ṛk-verses. Bhūvaḥ from the Yajus-texts , and Svaḥ from the Sāma-verses .—(3)

commentaries.author: Adi Shankaracharya Bhashya
commentaries.text: स एतां पुनरभ्यतपत् त्रयीं विद्याम् । तस्यास्तप्यमानाया रसं भूरिति व्याहृतिम् ऋग्भ्यो जग्राह ; भुवरिति व्याहृतिं यजुर्भ्यः ; स्वरिति व्याहृतिं सामभ्यः । अत एव लोकदेववेदरसा महाव्याहृतयः । अतः तत् तत्र यज्ञे यदि ऋक्तः ऋक्सम्बन्धादृङ्निमित्तं रिष्येत् यज्ञः क्षतं प्राप्नुयात् , भूः स्वाहेति गार्हपत्ये जुहुयात् । सा तत्र प्रायश्चित्तिः । कथम् ? ऋचामेव, तदिति क्रियाविशेषणम् , रसेन ऋचां विर्येण ओजसा ऋचां यज्ञस्य ऋक्सम्बन्धिनो यज्ञस्य विरिष्टं विच्छिन्नं क्षतरूपमुत्पन्नं सन्दधाति प्रतिसन्धत्ते ॥

commentaries.author: Adi Shankaracharya Bhashya (Translation)
commentaries.text: He again brooded over this Triadic Science —the Science of the three Vedas; from this Science, thus brooded over, He squeezed is essence ,— Bhūḥ ,—the first Vyāhṛti —from the Ṛk-verses,— Bhuvaḥ —the second Vyāhṛti —from the Yayuṣ-texts ,—and Svaḥ —the third Vyāhṛti — from the Sāma -verses ,—Thus these three Mahāvyāhṛtis Great Syllables ,—are the essence of all Regions , all Divinities and all Vedas .—At the several sacrificial performances, if the Sacrifice happen to become defective on any point relating to and on account of the Ṛk-Text, one should offer an oblation into the Gārhapatya fire , saying ‘ Bhūḥ Svāhā ’;—this is the extraction for the Defect.—How so? — Thus —this is an adverbial clause.— through the essence of the Ṛk-verses and the virility of the Ṛk-verses, one makes up the defect in the Sacrifice ;—i.e. heals up the wound that had been inflicted upon the Sacrifice, in relation to the Ṛk .—(3-4).

sanskrit_shloka: स यदि यजुष्टो रिष्येद्भुवः स्वाहेति दक्षिणाग्नौ जुहुयाद्यजुषामेव तद्रसेन यजुषां वीर्येण यजुषां यज्ञस्य विरिष्टं सन्दधाति ॥ ५ ॥
transliteration:
atha yadi yajuṣṭo riṣyed bhuvaḥ svāheti dakṣiṇāgnau juhuyāt |
               yajuṣām eva tadrasena yajuṣāṃ vīryeṇa yajuṣāṃ yajñasya viriṣṭaṃ saṃdadhāti || ChUp_4,17.5
               || atha yadi sāmato riṣyet svaḥ svāhety āhavanīye juhuyāt |
               sāmnām eva tadrasena sāmnāṃ vīryeṇa sāmnāṃ yajñasya viriṣṭaṃ saṃdadhāti || ChUp_4,17.6
               ||
translation: If the Sacrifice becomes defective in connection with the Yajus , one should offer an oblation into the Dakṣiṇāgni , saying ‘ Bhuvaḥ svāhā ’, and thus, through this essence of the Yajus Texts , and through the virility of the Yajus-texts , one makes up the defect of the Yajus-texts in the sacrifice.—(5)

translations.author: VedaPath English
translations.text: If the Sacrifice becomes defective in connection with the Yajus , one should offer an oblation into the Dakṣiṇāgni , saying ‘ Bhuvaḥ svāhā ’, and thus, through this essence of the Yajus Texts , and through the virility of the Yajus-texts , one makes up the defect of the Yajus-texts in the sacrifice.—(5)

commentaries.author: Adi Shankaracharya Bhashya (Translation)
commentaries.text:
If there be any defect related to, or caused by, the Yajus ,—one should offer an oblation into the Dakṣināgṇi , saying ‘ Bhuvaḥ svāhā ’;—similarly, when there is a defect due to Sāma, one should pour an oblation into the Āhavanīy a fire, saying ‘Svāḥ svāhā ’. In this way, as before, he makes up this defect in the Sacrifice.
When there is a defect due to the Brahman-Priest (as described above), one should offer three oblations into the three fires, pronouncing the three Vyāhṛtis (Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ and Svaḥ ); as such a defect would be a defect relating to all the three Vedas,—as declared in the Vedic Text—‘Now whereby is Brahman-hood attained? By means of the science of the three Vedas!’.—Or (if this is not found satisfactory) some other law will have to be found for rectifying the defect due to the Brahman-Priest .—(5-6).

sanskrit_shloka: अथ यदि सामतो रिष्येत्स्वः स्वाहेत्याहवनीये जुहुयात्साम्नामेव तद्रसेन साम्नां वीर्येण साम्नां यज्ञस्य विरिष्टं सन्दधाति ॥ ६ ॥
transliteration:
atha yadi yajuṣṭo riṣyed bhuvaḥ svāheti dakṣiṇāgnau juhuyāt |
               yajuṣām eva tadrasena yajuṣāṃ vīryeṇa yajuṣāṃ yajñasya viriṣṭaṃ saṃdadhāti || ChUp_4,17.5
               || atha yadi sāmato riṣyet svaḥ svāhety āhavanīye juhuyāt |
               sāmnām eva tadrasena sāmnāṃ vīryeṇa sāmnāṃ yajñasya viriṣṭaṃ saṃdadhāti || ChUp_4,17.6
               ||
translation: If the Sacrifice becomes defective in connection with the Yajus , one should offer an oblation into the Dakṣiṇāgni , saying ‘ Bhuvaḥ svāhā ’, and thus, through this essence of the Yajus Texts , and through the virility of the Yajus-texts , one makes up the defect of the Yajus-texts in the sacrifice.—(5)

translations.author: VedaPath English
translations.text: If the Sacrifice becomes defective in connection with the Yajus , one should offer an oblation into the Dakṣiṇāgni , saying ‘ Bhuvaḥ svāhā ’, and thus, through this essence of the Yajus Texts , and through the virility of the Yajus-texts , one makes up the defect of the Yajus-texts in the sacrifice.—(5)

commentaries.author: Adi Shankaracharya Bhashya
commentaries.text:
अथ यदि यजुष्टो यजुर्निमित्तं रिष्येत् , भुवः स्वाहेति दक्षिणाग्नौ जुहुयात् । तथा सामनिमित्ते रेषे स्वः स्वाहेत्याहवनीये जुहुयात् । तथा पूर्ववद्यज्ञं सन्दधाति । ब्रह्मनिमित्ते तु रेषे त्रिष्वग्निषु तिसृभिर्व्याहृतिभिर्जुहुयात् । त्रय्या हि विद्यायाः स रेषः, 
‘अथ केन ब्रह्मत्वमित्यनयैव त्रय्या विद्यया’ ( ? )
 इति श्रुतेः । न्यायान्तरं वा मृग्यं ब्रह्मत्वनिमित्ते रेषे ॥

commentaries.author: Adi Shankaracharya Bhashya (Translation)
commentaries.text:
If there be any defect related to, or caused by, the Yajus ,—one should offer an oblation into the Dakṣināgṇi , saying ‘ Bhuvaḥ svāhā ’;—similarly, when there is a defect due to Sāma, one should pour an oblation into the Āhavanīy a fire, saying ‘Svāḥ svāhā ’. In this way, as before, he makes up this defect in the Sacrifice.
When there is a defect due to the Brahman-Priest (as described above), one should offer three oblations into the three fires, pronouncing the three Vyāhṛtis (Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ and Svaḥ ); as such a defect would be a defect relating to all the three Vedas,—as declared in the Vedic Text—‘Now whereby is Brahman-hood attained? By means of the science of the three Vedas!’.—Or (if this is not found satisfactory) some other law will have to be found for rectifying the defect due to the Brahman-Priest .—(5-6).

sanskrit_shloka: तद्यथा लवणेन सुवर्णं सन्दध्यात्सुवर्णेन रजतं रजतेन त्रपु त्रपुणा सीसं सीसेन लोहं लोहेन दारु दारु चर्मणा ॥ ७ ॥
transliteration:
tad yathā lavaṇena suvarṇaṃ saṃdadhyāt |
               suvarṇena rajataṃ rajatena trapu trapuṇā sīsaṃ sīsena lohaṃ lohena dāru dāru carmaṇā
               || ChUp_4,17.7 || evam eṣāṃ lokānām āsāṃ devatānām asyās trayyā vidyāyā vīryeṇa yajñasya viriṣṭaṃ saṃdadhāti
               |
               bheṣajakṛto ha vā eṣa yajño yatraivaṃvid brahmā bhavati || ChUp_4,17.8 ||
translation: Just as one would join gold by salt, silver by gold, tin by silver, lead by tin, iron by lead, wood by iron, and wood by leather;—(7)

translations.author: VedaPath English
translations.text: Just as one would join gold by salt, silver by gold, tin by silver, lead by tin, iron by lead, wood by iron, and wood by leather;—(7)

commentaries.author: Adi Shankaracharya Bhashya (Translation)
commentaries.text: Just as one would join gold by salt , i.e. by Borax and such other salts, which serve to soften the hard gold-pieces,— silver by gold ,—silver, which is otherwise unjoinable, becomes joined by gold;— Tin by silver—lead by tin—iron by lead,—wood by iron,—and wood by leather ,— by leather-bandages—in this same way one makes good the defect in the Sacrifice, by the virility —i.e. force, called Essence —of the said Regions, Divinities and the Science of the three Vedas.—That sacrifice verily becomes well-healed up .—just as a sick patient becomes healthy through an expert physician,—so does that Sacrifice become,—which sacrifice?—That sacrifice at which there is a Brahman-Priest knowing this —i.e. who knows the expiatory rite, by means of the Vyāhṛtis .—(7-8).

sanskrit_shloka: एवमेषां लोकानामासां देवतानामस्यास्त्रय्या विद्याया वीर्येण यज्ञस्य विरिष्टं सन्दधाति भेषजकृतो ह वा एष यज्ञो यत्रैवंविद्ब्रह्मा भवति ॥ ८ ॥
transliteration:
tad yathā lavaṇena suvarṇaṃ saṃdadhyāt |
               suvarṇena rajataṃ rajatena trapu trapuṇā sīsaṃ sīsena lohaṃ lohena dāru dāru carmaṇā
               || ChUp_4,17.7 || evam eṣāṃ lokānām āsāṃ devatānām asyās trayyā vidyāyā vīryeṇa yajñasya viriṣṭaṃ saṃdadhāti
               |
               bheṣajakṛto ha vā eṣa yajño yatraivaṃvid brahmā bhavati || ChUp_4,17.8 ||
translation: Just as one would join gold by salt, silver by gold, tin by silver, lead by tin, iron by lead, wood by iron, and wood by leather;—(7)

translations.author: VedaPath English
translations.text: Just as one would join gold by salt, silver by gold, tin by silver, lead by tin, iron by lead, wood by iron, and wood by leather;—(7)

commentaries.author: Adi Shankaracharya Bhashya
commentaries.text: तद्यथा लवणेन सुवर्णं सन्दध्यात् । क्षारेण टङ्कणादिना खरे मृदुत्वकरं हि तत् । सुवर्णेन रजतमशक्यसन्धानं सन्दध्यात् । रजतेन तथा त्रपु, त्रपुणा सीसम् , सीसेन लोहम् , लोहेन दारु, दारु चर्मणा चर्मबन्धनेन । एवमेषां लोकानामासां देवतानामस्यास्त्रय्या विद्याया वीर्येण रसाख्येनौजसा यज्ञस्य विरिष्टं सन्दधाति । भेषजकृतो ह वा एष यज्ञः — रोगार्त इव पुमांश्चिकित्सकेन सुशिक्षितेन एष यज्ञो भवति । कोऽसौ ? यत्र यस्मिन्यज्ञे एवंवित् यथोक्तव्याहृतिहोमप्रायश्चित्तवित् ब्रह्मा ऋत्विग्भवति स यज्ञ इत्यर्थः ॥

commentaries.author: Adi Shankaracharya Bhashya (Translation)
commentaries.text: Just as one would join gold by salt , i.e. by Borax and such other salts, which serve to soften the hard gold-pieces,— silver by gold ,—silver, which is otherwise unjoinable, becomes joined by gold;— Tin by silver—lead by tin—iron by lead,—wood by iron,—and wood by leather ,— by leather-bandages—in this same way one makes good the defect in the Sacrifice, by the virility —i.e. force, called Essence —of the said Regions, Divinities and the Science of the three Vedas.—That sacrifice verily becomes well-healed up .—just as a sick patient becomes healthy through an expert physician,—so does that Sacrifice become,—which sacrifice?—That sacrifice at which there is a Brahman-Priest knowing this —i.e. who knows the expiatory rite, by means of the Vyāhṛtis .—(7-8).

sanskrit_shloka: एष ह वा उदक्प्रवणो यज्ञो यत्रैवंविद्ब्रह्मा भवत्येवंविदं ह वा एषा ब्रह्माणमनुगाथा यतो यत आवर्तते तत्तद्गच्छति ॥ ९ ॥
transliteration:
eṣa ha vā udakpravaṇo yajño yatraivaṃvid brahmā bhavati |
               evaṃvidaṃ ha vā eṣā brahmāṇam anu gāthā |
               yato yata āvartate tat tad gacchati || ChUp_4,17.9 ||
translation: That Sacrifice indeed is ‘North-sloping’ where there is a Brahman-Priest knowing this. It is in reference to the Brahman-Priest knowing this that there is the saying that ‘Wherever it fails, there he goes’.—(9)

translations.author: VedaPath English
translations.text: That Sacrifice indeed is ‘North-sloping’ where there is a Brahman-Priest knowing this. It is in reference to the Brahman-Priest knowing this that there is the saying that ‘Wherever it fails, there he goes’.—(9)

commentaries.author: Adi Shankaracharya Bhashya
commentaries.text: किं च, एष ह वा उदक्प्रवण उदङ्निम्नो दक्षिणोच्छ्रायो यज्ञो भवति ; उत्तरमार्गप्रतिपत्तिहेतुरित्यर्थः । यत्रैवंविद्ब्रह्मा भवति । एवंविदं ह वै ब्रह्माणम् ऋत्विजं प्रति एषा अनुगाथा ब्रह्मणः स्तुतिपरा — यतो यत आवर्तते कर्म प्रदेशात् ऋत्विजां यज्ञः क्षतीभवन् , तत्तद्यज्ञस्य क्षतरूपं प्रतिसन्दधत् प्रायश्चित्तेन गच्छति परिपालयतीत्येतत् ॥

commentaries.author: Adi Shankaracharya Bhashya (Translation)
commentaries.text: Further, that sacrifice is ‘North-sloping ’— rising towards the South,—i.e. it becomes the means of reaching the Northern Path,— where there is a Brahman Priest knowing this; that there is this saying —eulogising the Brahman-Priest —‘Wherever it—the action. Sacrifice-fails i.e. from whatever part of the Priests the Sacrifice suffers harm , becomes defective—that defect of the Sacrifice he heals up by means of the expiatory Rite,— and there he goes ,—i.e. he protects the Sacrifice.—(9).

sanskrit_shloka: मानवो ब्रह्मैवैक ऋत्विक्कुरूनश्वाभिरक्षत्येवंविद्ध वै ब्रह्मा यज्ञं यजमानं सर्वांश्चर्त्विजोऽभिरक्षति तस्मादेवंविदमेव ब्रह्माणं कुर्वीत नानेवंविदं नानेवंविदम् ॥ १० ॥
transliteration:
mānavo brahmaivaika ṛtvikkurūnaśvābhirakṣatyevaṃviddha vai brahmā yajñaṃ yajamānaṃ
               sarvāṃś cartvijo 'bhirakṣati tasmādevaṃvidameva brahmāṇaṃ kurvīta nānevaṃvidaṃ nānevaṃvidam
               //10// mānavaḥ |
               brahmaivaika ṛtvik kurūn aśvābhirakṣati |
               evaṃvid dha vai brahmā yajñaṃ yajamānaṃ sarvāṃś cartvijo 'bhirakṣati |
               tasmād evaṃvidam eva brahmāṇaṃ kurvīta nānevaṃvidaṃ nānevaṃvidam || ChUp_4,17.10 ||
translation: The silent Brahman is the one priest who protects the performers, like the Mare. The Brahman-Priest who knows this protects the Sacrifice, the Sacrificer, and all the priests. Hence one should have as Brahman Priest only one who knows this,—not one who knows this not,—yea, knows it not—(10).

translations.author: VedaPath English
translations.text: The silent Brahman is the one priest who protects the performers, like the Mare. The Brahman-Priest who knows this protects the Sacrifice, the Sacrificer, and all the priests. Hence one should have as Brahman Priest only one who knows this,—not one who knows this not,—yea, knows it not—(10).

commentaries.author: Adi Shankaracharya Bhashya
commentaries.text: मानवो ब्रह्मा मौनाचरणान्मननाद्वा ज्ञानवत्त्वात् ; ततो ब्रह्मैवैकः ऋत्विक् कुरून् कर्तॄन् — योद्धॄनारूढानश्वा बडबा यथा अभिरक्षति, एवंवित् ह वै ब्रह्मा यज्ञं यजमानं सर्वांश्च ऋत्विजोऽभिरक्षति, तत्कृतदोषापनयनात् । यत एवं विशिष्टो ब्रह्मा विद्वान् , तस्मादेवंविदमेव यथोक्तव्याहृत्यादिविदं ब्रह्माणं कुर्वीत, नानेवंविदं कदाचनेति । द्विरभ्यासोऽध्यायपरिसमाप्त्यर्थः ॥

commentaries.author: Adi Shankaracharya Bhashya (Translation)
commentaries.text:
The silent Brahman —called ‘ Mānava ’ because he has taken the vow of silence, or because he is possessed of right knowledge,— is the only one priest who protects the performers ,—just as the Horse protects its rider.— The Brahman-priest who knows this protects the Sacrifice, the Sacrificer, and all the priests —by removing the defects caused by them. Inasmuch as the Brahman should be so learned one should have as Brahman one who knows the Vyāḥrtis and other details described above,— and never one who knows not this .—The repetition is meant to indicate the end of the Discourse.—(10)
End of Section (17) of Discourse IV
End of Discourse IV .
